summary: Missing "warm-cache" reserved credits on invoice due to postback tag omission
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that monthly invoice for Feb 2026 shows full dynamic usage charges for a subset of streaming requests that should have been classified as 'warm-cache' reserved usage and thus eligible for reserved credits. Impact: NovaDocs reports a $3,125.00 unexpected charge on their finalized invoice; this is blocking autopay and triggering an account hold. Environment: private deployment (VPC) in us-east-1; customer runs a multi-model pipeline that warms KV/prefix cache during short-lived canary traffic. Observed behavior: Postback records for warmup requests arrive without the 'warm_cache' usage_tag, so billing pipeline attributes them as on-demand streaming tokens rather than reserved warmup usage. Expected behavior: Warmup requests should be tagged with 'warm_cache' in postbacks and consumed from the customer's reserved capacity pool, reducing billed on-demand tokens. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run canary traffic hitting /v1/chat/stream with header X-Redwood-Warmup: true from NovaDocs private endpoint. 2) Inspect outgoing usage postbacks at postback service (postback logs show no warm_cache tag for many warmup requests). 3) Compare postback payloads to billing classification logs and invoice line items. Supporting logs and artifacts: postback samples (linked), billing classification trace for invoice lines, sandbox reproduction playbook at confluence link. Time window: Feb 26 2026 02:00 - Feb 27 2026 08:00 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a canary job that performs KV/prefix cache warmup on private endpoint
Capture outgoing usage postbacks from the postback-processor in the same time window
Compare the 'usage_tag' field across warmup vs normal requests
Run billing classification job locally against the captured postbacks to observe classification result
logs: postback-processor stderr snippet: "WARN missing usage_tag for request id=7f3a2d"
billing-classifier trace: invoice_line_id=inv_2026_02_26 severity=info classification=on_demand (should be warm_cache)
serving-runtime debug: route=canary warmup=true kv_cache_hit=false seq=1
customer_notes: Customer says: 'We intentionally run brief warmup bursts to avoid cold-start latency; we expected those to be charged against our reserved warmup buffer.'
Customer urgency: High — hold on autopay until corrected

proposed_workaround: Until the hotfix is fully deployed, advise the customer to enable a short-lived alternate header X-Redwood-Force-Warmup=1 on their warmup requests which forces explicit warmup classification in the postback service (server-side bypass). Support has provided bypass instructions to NovaDocs.
resolution: Pending — hotfix merged and rolling out. Billing will issue a provisional credit of $3,125.00 once post-deploy verification confirms tags are restored for historical replay. Final credit will be reconciled after a replay-based verification job completes (expected within 72 hours).
final_notes: Follow-up tasks: 1) INT-4421 to remain open until replay verification completes and credit memo is posted. 2) Add automated telemetry alert when usage_tag drop rate >0.1% for any customer. 3) Postmortem to document schema change guardrails and add contract tests for usage_tag presence.
